item.title: The Synaptic Polarity Flip: SCN2A Age-Bifurcation, GABAA & GRIN (NMDA) Channelopathies — One-Ångström cryo-EM walks inside human NaV1.2 (6J8E), α1β3γ2L GABAA with GABA & diazepam (6HUP), and GluN1-GluN2B NMDA with S-ketamine (7EU8) vs. memantine (7SAD); Bayesian <3-mo SCN2A & Woodhull Mg2+ pauses; phenytoin, vigabatrin hypersensitivity, L-serine, memantine, elsunersen, radiprodil & adolescent CRISPRa
item.description: Wave 10 Channelopathies Episode 8 (Ep 2668 / CHAN_08): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical and biophysical treatise uniting the synaptic gain-of-function vs. loss-of-function polarity flip across SCN2A/NaV1.2 (<3-month neonatal GoF rescued by high-dose phenytoin vs. >3-month LoF ASD/late spasms worsened by sodium-channel blockers + p.Arg853Gln DII-S4 gating-pore/LoF paradox), GABAA (GABRB3 GoF vigabatrin hypersensitivity [Absalom et al. 2020/2022] vs. GABRA1/GABRB3/GABRG2 LoF trafficking/NMD escape [Macdonald/Kang; Johannesen; Maillard 2022; Zhou 2022; Liu 2023]), and GRIN/NMDA (GRIN1/GRIN2A/GRIN2B GoF polymicrogyria & DEE treated with memantine/radiprodil vs. GRIN LoF & epilepsy-aphasia rescued by oral L-serine 500 mg/kg/day). Walks at 1 Å through verified RCSB PDB structures 6J8E (3.0 Å NaV1.2-β2-KIIIA), 6HUP (3.58 Å α1β3γ2L GABAA-GABA-DZP-PIP2), 7EU8 (4.07 Å GluN1-GluN2B-S-ketamine), and 7SAD (3.96 Å GluN1a-GluN2B-memantine); includes two spoken calculation pauses (Bayesian <3-mo SCN2A polarity LR + mature pyramidal Kv-AHP hyperexcitability paradox; Woodhull NMDA Mg2+ block at -70 vs -20 mV & memantine vs. ATD-allosteric radiprodil); and integrates verified clinical trials (EMBRAVE NCT05737784/NCT07019922 elsunersen, EMBOLD NCT05818553 relutrigine, nL-SCN2A-002 NCT06314490, Honeycomb NCT05818943 & Beeline NCT07224581 radiprodil, NCT07941206, TAP-GRIN NCT07377032 L-serine) plus Tamura/Ahituv/Bender Nature 2025 adolescent SCN2A CRISPRa rescue.

item.title: Storms Across the Cortex, Stumbles in the Cerebellum, and the Startle That Stops Breath: FHM1/FHM2, Episodic Ataxias & Hereditary Hyperekplexia — One-Ångström cryo-EM/X-ray walks inside human P/Q-type CaV2.1 (8X90), full-length Shaker Kv1.2 (3LUT), and open α1 Glycine Receptor (6PM6), Ca²⁺ fourth-power cooperativity & 3 mm/min CSD math, 4-AP/EAT-2-TREAT, Vigevano maneuver, niflumic acid Kv1.1 activation, and Phase 3 N-acetyl-L-leucine (NCT07221292)
item.description: Wave 10 Channelopathies Episode 9 (Ep 2669 / CHAN_09): Complete 5-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical and biophysical treatise uniting Familial Hemiplegic Migraine (FHM1 CACNA1A GoF R192Q/S218L/T666M, FHM2 ATP1A2 glial Na+/K+-ATPase LoF, FHM3 SCN1A GoF), Episodic Ataxias (EA1 KCNA1 Kv1.1 LoF with interictal myokymia vs. EA2 CACNA1A LoF with downbeat nystagmus and SCA6 exon-47 polyQ / bicistronic alpha1ACT), and Hereditary Hyperekplexia (GLRA1/GLRB/SLC6A5 stiff-baby startle apnea rescued by Vigevano maneuver & clonazepam). Anchored to direct coordinate measurements from RCSB PDB 8X90 (2.95 Å human CaV2.1 with CA2604, PS1, PT5 PIP2, and -1 DII offset at THR665 = canonical Thr666), 3LUT (2.9 Å full-length Shaker Kv1.2-Kvbeta2 with K500-K504, TVGYG, ARG294, S6 PVP +2 offset vs Kv1.1 V408A, and NAP368), and 6PM6 (2.9 Å open alpha1 GlyR bound to GLY504 with transparent +16 zebrafish-to-mature-human and +28 precursor HGVS numbering map: ARG287 = mature Arg271 19'-Arg, LEU277 = mature Leu261 9'-Leu, PRO266 = mature Pro250 -2'). Includes two spoken calculation pauses (presynaptic Ca2+ n=4 cooperativity 1.25^4 = 2.44x and 3 mm/min CSD 20-30 min occipital-to-motor march vs embolic stroke), RCT evidence (Strupp 2011, EAT-2-TREAT 2021), Servettini PNAS 2023 NFA Kv1.1 activation, Aldhilan 2022 & Dolu 2024 hyperekplexia cohorts, and verified ClinicalTrials.gov anchors (NCT07221292, NCT00266760, NCT01470729, NCT00358839, NCT00687947, NCT00257985, NCT00541736, NCT05687474).

item.title: The Burning-Pain Mirror: Inherited Erythromelalgia (IEM), Paroxysmal Extreme Pain Disorder (PEPD), TRPA1 FEPS & NaV1.8 Selective Analgesia (Suzetrigine) — One-Ångström cryo-EM walks inside human NaV1.7 (7W9K), NaV1.8 (7WFW/7WE4), and TRPA1 (6V9W/6PQO), Waxman's sympathetic-nociceptor NaV1.8 paradox, SCN11A L811P vs. L811F, carbamazepine in PEPD & S241T, suzetrigine (VX-548), BHV-7000, and AAV9 NaV1.7 epigenetic repression
item.description: Wave 10 Channelopathies Episode 10 (Ep 2670): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical and biophysical treatise on peripheral pain channelopathies (SCN9A Inherited Erythromelalgia IEM and Paroxysmal Extreme Pain Disorder PEPD, SCN10A/SCN11A small-fiber neuropathy and FEPS including the SCN11A p.Leu811Pro CIP vs. p.Leu811Phe FEPS codon-811 fork, and TRPA1 p.Asn855Ser FEPS1 including 2026 Schwann-cell 4-HNE signaling) plus NaV1.8 VSD2-selective non-opioid analgesia (suzetrigine / VX-548 / Journavx, approved 30 Jan 2025). Anchored to five verified RCSB PDB cryo-EM structures (7W9K with transparent +11 exon 11A offset in DII-DIV, 7WFW, 7WE4, 6V9W, 6PQO), two spoken calculation pauses (DRG Boltzmann -12 mV shift & sympathetic NaV1.8 depolarization-block paradox; suzetrigine free plasma target occupancy at NaV1.8 vs. cardiac NaV1.5), verified ClinicalTrials.gov studies (NAVIGATE 1/2 NCT05553366/NCT05558410, NCT05818852, NCT06628908, NCT02214615, NCT07262268, NCT05917912, NCT01769274, NCT02917187, NCT04039633), and emerging Kv7.2/7.3 bypass openers and AAV9 ZFP-KRAB NaV1.7 epigenetic silencing.

item.title: When the Folding Clock Breaks: Cystic Fibrosis (CFTR Classes I-VI), Trikafta & Alyftrek Rescue, and the Modulator-Ineligible 10% Frontier — One-Ångström cryo-EM walks inside human CFTR (5UAK apo, 6MSM ATP-dimerized, 8EIQ ΔF508 bound to tezacaftor CV6, elexacaftor WJX & ivacaftor VX7), sweat-duct vs. airway Cl-/HCO3- & NPD physics, ΔΔG folding math, SKYLINE/RIDGELINE Alyftrek, and Class I mRNA/AAV/ACE-tRNA/prime editing
item.description: Wave 10 Channelopathies Episode 11 (Ep 2671 / CHAN_11): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical and biophysical treatise on Cystic Fibrosis (CFTR / ABCC7 Classes I-VI), contrasting severe newborn F508del/F508del meconium ileus (sweat Cl- 104 mmol/L), adult R117H-5T CBAVD/recurrent pancreatitis (sweat Cl- 42 mmol/L), and modulator-ineligible Class I G542X/W1282X; tracing Dorothy Andersen (1938), Paul di Sant'Agnese (1953), Gibson & Cooke (1959), Paul Quinton (1983), Tsui/Riordan/Collins (1989), Beekman rectal organoid FIS (2013), and Jue Chen's human CFTR cryo-EM trilogy (PDB 5UAK, 6MSM, 8EIQ with CV6 tezacaftor, WJX elexacaftor, VX7 ivacaftor); featuring two spoken calculation pauses (sweat-duct vs. airway Cl-/HCO3- polarity, Henderson-Hasselbalch ASL pH 7.20->6.62 & NPD Wilschanski index; Boltzmann ddG folding synergy & multiplicative N_surf x P_o rescue math), verified Phase 3 evidence (Ramsey 2011, Wainwright 2015, Middleton 2019, Heijerman 2019, Mall 2022, Burgel 2024, SKYLINE 102/103 & RIDGELINE 2025), One Medicine CF pig/ferret proofs, and verified Class I 10% frontier trials (NCT05668741 VX-522, NCT06237335 RCT2100, NCT05248230 4D-710, NCT06526923 SP-101, NCT06515002/NCT06962852 BI 3720931, Ahern ACE-tRNAs, Bulcaen 2024 prime editing).

item.title: Salt, Sugar, and One Broken Atom: Renal Tubular (Bartter, Gitelman, EAST/SeSAME, PHA1) & Endocrine K_ATP Neonatal Diabetes / DEND Channelopathies — Genetic lifelong furosemide vs. thiazide (+8 mV TAL paracellular Ca2+ physics, urine Cl-/Ca2+/Cr triage & MLPA), EAST/SeSAME Kir4.1 vs. Kir5.1, PHA1 vs. Liddle ENaC mirrors, One-Ångström cryo-EM walks inside human NCC (8FHT, 8VPN + indapamide/WNK-SPAK) and pancreatic K_ATP (6BAA + glibenclamide, 6C3O + MgADP), and high-dose oral sulfonylurea transfer freeing 93% of KCNJ11 children from insulin needles
item.description: Wave 10 Channelopathies Episode 12 (Ep 2672): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical and biophysical treatise uniting Renal Tubular Channelopathies (Antenatal/Classic Bartter Types I–V [SLC12A1/NKCC2, KCNJ1/ROMK transient neonatal hyperkalemia, CLCNKB, BSND/Barttin deafness, MAGED2], Gitelman Syndrome [SLC12A3/NCC, 6% Alu MLPA rearrangements, Gordon/FHHt WNK-SPAK mirror], EAST/SeSAME [KCNJ10/Kir4.1 vs. KCNJ16/Kir5.1 acidosis], and Systemic PHA1B [SCNN1A/B/G ENaC LoF mirror of Liddle Syndrome]) with the Endocrine K_ATP Mirror (KCNJ11/ABCC8 GoF Permanent Neonatal Diabetes & iDEND/DEND Syndrome vs. Congenital Hyperinsulinism). Grounded in four verified RCSB PDB cryo-EM structures (8FHT [3.02 Å human NCC + Na+/Cl-], 8VPN [2.7 Å phosphorylated human NCC + indapamide BL1 + WNK-SPAK TPO55/TPO60/SEP73 + CTD ATP, -1 isoform numbering offset], 6BAA [3.63 Å Kir6.2/SUR1 K_ATP + ATP + glibenclamide GBM at ARG1246 2.80 Å], and 6C3O [3.9 Å human K_ATP quatrefoil + K+ TIGFG + SUR1 MgADP 1.89 Å / MgATP 1.98 Å]), two spoken calculation pauses (+8 mV lumen-positive TAL paracellular divalent Boltzmann factor & uCa/uCr + uCl- differential; p.Arg201His 30x IC50(ATP) shift locking beta-cell V_m at -80.7 mV and 0.5-1.5 mg/kg/day glibenclamide transfer physics with zero severe hypoglycemia), all 15 dossier PMIDs / 10 PMCIDs, and all 14 verified ClinicalTrials.gov NCT trials (NCT02624817 10-year 93% durable insulin independence, NCT00334711, NCT02624830, NCT05751525, NCT02921906, NCT00321321, NCT06065852, NCT03847571, NCT04995627, NCT01146197, NCT00822107, NCT00276289, NCT02297048, NCT02035046).

item.title: Beyond Action Potentials: Immune, Auditory, Retinal & Mechanosensitive Rare Channelopathies — One-Ångström cryo-EM & X-ray walks inside hexameric Orai (4HKR), Connexin-26 (2ZW3), native TMC-1 (7USW), pentameric BEST1 (6N26), cone CNGA3/CNGB3-cGMP (8EV8), and 114-TM PIEZO2 (6KG7), ~20 fS CRAC vs. +80 mV endocochlear physics, urgent HSCT, subretinal AAV-CNGA3/CNGB3, intracochlear AAV-GJB2/TMC1, and zegocractin
item.description: Wave 10 Channelopathies Episode 13 (Ep 2673): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical and biophysical treatise on immune, auditory, retinal, and mechanosensitive rare channelopathies — contrasting ORAI1 p.Arg91Trp / STIM1 LoF T+B+NK+ CRAC SCID (normal flow cytometry & TRECs, hypotonia, anhidrosis, amelogenesis imperfecta; cured immunologically by HSCT while non-hematopoietic organs persist) against dominant STIM1 p.Arg304Trp / ORAI1 GoF Stormorken Syndrome & Tubular Aggregate Myopathy; GJB2 (Cx26 c.35delG, p.Met34Thr, p.Val37Ile) cochlear K+ recycling deafness against TMC1 (DFNB7/11 & DFNA36) hair-cell MET pore deafness; CNGA3/CNGB3 achromatopsia (flat photopic ERG, normal scotopic rod ERG) against BEST1 Best vitelliform macular dystrophy & ARB (egg-yolk macula, bilateral depressed EOG Arden ratio <1.5 even in unilateral fundus presentations); and PIEZO2 LoF proprioception/vibration/bladder-stretch absence (Chesler & Bönnemann NEJM 2016) against GoF Distal Arthrogryposis Type 5 / Marden-Walker Syndrome. Walks at 1 Å inside verified PDBs 4HKR, 2ZW3, 7USW, 6N26, 8EV8, and 6KG7; includes two spoken calculation pauses (~20 fS single-channel Orai1 conductance & 5,000-10,000 channel STIM1 puncta NFAT accumulation; +80 mV endocochlear potential & 150 mV TMC1 driving force conducting 15,000x faster than Orai1); and integrates verified ClinicalTrials.gov trials (NCT02610582, NCT03758404, NCT03001310, NCT02599922, NCT02935517, NCT03278873, NCT04124185, NCT01648452, NCT07941115 SENS-601, NCT07627971 SKY-GJB2, NCT05402813, NCT05788536 DB-OTO, NCT05821959 AK-OTOF, NCT06370351 SENS-501, NCT03401190, NCT04681066 CARPO, NCT04345614 CARDEA, NCT06374797 KOURAGE).

item.title: Beyond the Outer Membrane and Beyond the Genome: Organellar (TRPML1, ClC-7/Ostm1), TRPV4 Neuro-Skeletal & LGI1/CASPR2/AQP4 Autoimmune Channelopathies — One-Ångström atomic walks inside human TRPML1 ± PI(3,5)P2 (5WJ5/6E7P), ClC-7/Ostm1 (7JM7), TRPV4–RhoA–GSK2798745 (8FC7), and Aquaporin-4 (3GD8); osteoclast +150 mV V-ATPase stall & TRPV4/LGI1 NNT physics; NMOSD biologics, AAV9.hMCOLN1co (NCT07398872), GSK2798745 repurposing, allele-specific CLCN7 siRNA & BCMA/CD19 CAR-T
item.description: Wave 10 Channelopathies Finale (Episode CHAN_14 / Ep 2674): Complete five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical and biophysical treatise covering lysosomal MCOLN1/TRPML1 (Mucolipidosis IV, constitutive achlorhydria & gastrin >1,000 pg/mL), lysosomal/osteoclast CLCN7/OSTM1 (ARO, dominant Albers-Schönberg ADO2 & 2024 gain-of-function HOD syndrome via PI(3,5)P2 unbraking), TRPV4 gain-of-function bifurcating via RhoA tethering between CMT2C vocal-cord neuropathy and metatropic skeletal dysplasia, and autoimmune-phenocopy channelopathies (Anti-LGI1 FBDS + SIADH, Anti-CASPR2 Morvan/Isaacs neuromyotonia + thymoma, and Anti-AQP4 NMOSD + MS-drug worsening trap). Walks at 1 Å inside verified RCSB PDBs 5WJ5, 6E7P, 7JM7, 8FC7, and 3GD8; includes two spoken calculation pauses (osteoclast lacunar pH 4.5 +150 mV V-ATPase stall & 2 Cl- : 1 H+ lysosomal Cl- equilibrium; TRPV4 R269H axonal Ca2+ overload vs GSK2798745 & Anti-LGI1 immunotherapy vs ASM NNT); covers PREVENT/CHAMPION-NMOSD/N-MOmentum/SAkuraSky/SAkuraStar biologics, urgent HSCT neuronopathic contraindications, and emerging therapies anchored to verified ClinicalTrials.gov trials (NCT07398872 AAV9.hMCOLN1co, NCT05782387, NCT05503264 satralizumab in LGI1, NCT06510283 telitacicept, NCT06515106, NCT02135861), allele-specific CLCN7 siRNA, FcRn blockers, and BCMA/CD19 CAR-T.

item.title: When the Heart Forgets How to Reset: Congenital Long QT Syndrome (LQT1, LQT2, LQT3 & Jervell-Lange-Nielsen) — One-Ångström cryo-EM walks inside human KCNQ1-KCNE1-PIP2 (9VEC/9VEI), hERG (5VA1/7CN1), and NaV1.5 (6UZ3/7DTC), Bazett vs. Fridericia & late-I_NaL physics, nadolol, mexiletine in LQT2, lumacaftor-ivacaftor, and SupRep AAV9 gene therapy
item.description: Wave 10 Channelopathies Episode 1 (Ep 2661): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical and biophysical treatise on Congenital Long QT Syndrome (LQT1 KCNQ1/KCNE1, LQT2 KCNH2/hERG, LQT3 SCN5A) and Jervell-Lange-Nielsen deafness-QT syndrome, anchored to verified RCSB PDB structures 9VEC, 9VEI, 5VA1, 7CN1, 6UZ3 (+1 DI / +2 DIV rat offset), and 7DTC, two spoken worked calculation pauses (Bazett vs. Fridericia; late-I_NaL plateau charge transfer & Nernst E_K hypokalemia paradox), verified ClinicalTrials.gov trials (NCT04581408, NCT02365532, NCT02300558, NCT03291145, NCT02082431, NCT02814981, NCT03841838, NCT06546137), and emerging SupRep AAV9 gene therapy.

item.title: The Fever That Unmasks the Notch: Brugada Syndrome & SCN5A Overlap — Brugada Syndrome, Lenègre/PCCD & LQT3/BrS Overlap, Fever Q10 Unmasking, Ajmaline/Flecainide Provocation Bayesian PPV, Quinidine I_to Rescue & RVOT Epicardial Ablation (PDB 6UZ3, 6UZ0, 6LQA, 7DTC)
item.description: 5-Act One-Ångström-Tall Man Channelopathy Treatise covering nocturnal agonal respiration, Southeast Asian SUNDS/Lai Tai/Bangungut, high-precordial 2nd/3rd ICS ECG unmasking, Shanghai Score, Brugadadrugs.org hazards, Brugada phenocopies, Depolarization vs Repolarization mechanisms, cross-ancestry polygenic GWAS (Barc 2022, Ishikawa 2024), SCN5A overlap polarity (Lenègre/PCCD, E1784K, MEPPC G213D), 1-Å cryo-EM walk through PDB 6UZ3/6UZ0/6LQA/7DTC, Bayesian ajmaline PPV & fever Q10/I_to dome-collapse Calculation Pauses, ICD stratification, oral hydroquinidine, epicardial RVOT ablation (NCT02641431, BRAVO NCT04420078), and emerging Kv4.3/MOG1/Empagliflozin (NCT07146880) frontiers.

item.title: Calcium Storms, Webbed Hands & the Three-Gene Paradox: Timothy, Andersen-Tawil, Short QT & Calmodulin CPVT — Multi-Organ Cardiac-Brain-Limb Channelopathies: Timothy Syndrome (CACNA1C LQT8), Andersen-Tawil Syndrome (KCNJ2 LQT7), Short QT Syndrome (SQTS) & Recessive/Calmodulin CPVT (CASQ2 / CALM1–3 / RyR2) (PDB 8WE6, 7ZDZ, 7UA5, 6XY3)
item.description: 5-Act One-Ångström-Tall Man Channelopathy Treatise covering multi-organ Timothy Syndrome (CACNA1C exon 8A p.Gly406Arg syndactyly, 2:1 functional AV block, fasting hypoglycemia, autism, 2025 Delphi consensus), Andersen-Tawil Syndrome (KCNJ2 Kir2.1 giant QU-waves, bidirectional VT, periodic paralysis, micrognathia/clinodactyly), Short QT Syndrome (SQT1–SQT6 desert-tent T-waves, hydroquinidine vs sotalol failure, ICD T-wave oversensing), and recessive CASQ2/TRDN + de novo CALM1–3 calmodulinopathy CPVT/LQTS (epinephrine storm trap, ICD shock storms, parental mosaicism). Features 1-Å walks through PDB 8WE6, 7ZDZ, 7UA5, and 6XY3, two spoken Calculation Pauses (exon-8A 11.5% Ca2+ overload & 1-(5/6)^4 calmodulin tetramer poisoning), nadolol/flecainide/LCSD (NCT01117454), Pașca's Nature 2024 TS1-ASO (NCT07600658), Bortolin 2024 CALM1-depleting ASO, AAV9-CASQ2 (>=33% threshold), Rycal ARM210, and Phase 2 CaMKII inhibitor CRD-4730 (NCT06658899).

item.title: The Double-Barreled Chloride Shunt: Myotonia Congenita — CLCN1 Thomsen AD vs. Becker AR, Double-Barreled ClC-1 Gate, T-Tubule Potassium Trapping, Fournier Pattern II EMG, Mexiletine vs. Lamotrigine, and One Medicine Tennessee Fainting Goats (PDB 6COY, 6QVU)
item.description: One-Ångström-Tall Man Channelopathy Treatise (Ep 2664): Five-act bedside-to-cryo-EM deep dive into CLCN1 Myotonia Congenita (dominant Thomsen AD vs. recessive Becker AR), One Medicine Tennessee myotonic goats (p.Ala885Pro) & miniature Schnauzers, human ClC-1 cryo-EM structures PDB 6COY (3.36 Å) & PDB 6QVU (4.2 Å, low pH + CBS domains), two worked calculation pauses (30-nm T-tubule K+ trapping/GHK depolarization and dimer binomial dominant-negative probability), Fournier Pattern II vs. I/III EMG, perioperative succinylcholine safety, mexiletine (Statland/Stunnenberg/MYOMEX) vs. lamotrigine (Andersen), and future ClC-1 allosteric potentiators & RNA-seq splice diagnostics.

item.title: The Leak Through the Voltage Sensor: Periodic Paralyses & Paramyotonia Congenita — HypoPP (CACNA1S/SCN4A), HyperPP, Paramyotonia Congenita & the S4 Gating-Pore Omega (ω) Current Revolution (PDB 6AGF, 6JPA, 6C1K)
item.description: One-Ångström-Tall Man Channelopathy Treatise (Ep 2665 / CHAN_05): Contrasts HypoPP1 (CACNA1S R528H/R1239H) & HypoPP2 (SCN4A R669H/R672H/G/S) resting S4 gating-pore omega currents against HyperPP (SCN4A T704M/M1592V persistent I_NaP), cold-aggravated Eulenburg Paramyotonia Congenita (SCN4A R1448C/H), equine HYPP (Impressive Phe1416Leu), and Thyrotoxic PP (KCNJ18/Kir2.6). Walks at 1 Å through human NaV1.4-β1 (PDB 6AGF), CaV1.1-verapamil (PDB 6JPA), and NavAb(R2G)-guanidinium (PDB 6C1K); includes two spoken calculation pauses (paradoxical low-K+ Kir2.1 bistable depolarization & McManis LET peak-to-nadir CMAP decrement) and verified trial evidence (NCT00004802, HYP-HOP/Sansone 2021, Ciafaloni 2019, NCT02582476 bumetanide, NCT05639257 lamotrigine vs Namuscla, NCT06917430 AI muscle MRI).

item.title: Two Gates on One Muscle Fiber: Slow vs. Fast CMS & RYR1 Core Myopathies — Slow-Channel vs. Fast-Channel nAChR Kinetic Polarity, Double-CMAP & Pyridostigmine Contraindication Minefield (SCCMS, COLQ, DOK7), Fluoxetine/Quinidine Open-Channel Block, 3,4-DAP, Oral Salbutamol Fold Remodeling, Fetal Gamma-to-Epsilon Switch & Congenital RYR1 Core Myopathies vs. Malignant Hyperthermia With Cooperative ARM210/ATP Rycal Stabilization (PDB 9DMG, 9DMH, 7TZC)
item.description: 5-Act One-Ångström-Tall Man Channelopathy Treatise uniting Gate One (human adult muscle nAChR α2βδε in apo PDB 9DMG [2.05 Å] and ACh-bound PDB 9DMH [2.06 Å], Li et al., Cell 2025, PMID 40203823) and Gate Two (2.2-MDa RyR1–calstabin1–CaM–ARM210–ATP–caffeine–Ca2+–Zn2+ complex PDB 7TZC [2.45 Å], Melville et al., Structure 2022, PMID 35580609). Covers three bedside clinical vignettes (SCCMS double-CMAP wrist-extensor drop worsened by pyridostigmine; FCCMS/CHRNE infantile apnea rescued by pyridostigmine + 3,4-DAP vs. COLQ and DOK7 paradoxically worsened by pyridostigmine; congenital RYR1 core myopathy vs. acute MH), historical giants (Engel, Sine, Beeson, Yamanashi, Shy & Magee, fetal γ→ε switch), exact measured 1-Å geometries (α1 TRP149 cation-π box, αGLY153–PRO197 1.75→2.40 Å Loop B–C spring, εPRO121 2.57 Å FCCMS wall, M2 9'-Leu LEU251 6.98→9.57 Å pore expansion, εLEU269 2.22→1.76 Å SCCMS latch, RyR1 RY1&2 KVR5306–ATP5305 2.97 Å cooperative Rycal pocket), two spoken calculation pauses (30x subsynaptic Ca2+ excitotoxicity in SCCMS + pyridostigmine; neuromuscular safety factor EPP/ΔV_thresh collapse in FCCMS vs. DOK7 during 3 Hz RNS), precision clinical-polarity pharmacology, and active trials (NCT04141670, NCT07560020 Surlorian/ARM210, NCT06436742 ARGX-119, NCT07830563 AMP-101 AAV-DOK7, NCT02562066 amifampridine).

item.title: The Subthreshold Brake and the Migrating Storm: KCNQ2/KCNQ3 (M-Current) & KCNT1 (Slack) Epileptic Encephalopathies — Neonatal KCNQ2 LoF Tonic Storms vs. SeLFNE vs. R201C/H GoF Hypoventilation, KCNT1 EIMFS Migrating Hemispheres & ADSHE, One-Ångström Cryo-EM Walks Inside KCNQ2 S5 Trp236–Retigabine (7CR0/7CR2) and Slo2.2 RCK1/RCK2 Gating Ring (5U70/5U76), M-Current Tetramer & Quinidine-vs-hERG Calculations, Azetukalner (XEN1101), BHV-7000, ABS-1230 (KYRON), and S230815 ASO (KANDLE)
item.description: Wave 10 Channelopathies Episode 7 (Ep 2667): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical and biophysical treatise contrasting KCNQ2/KCNQ3 (Kv7.2/7.3 M-current: SeLFNE haploinsufficient LoF, dominant-negative KCNQ2-DEE neonatal asymmetric tonic storms, and S4 R201C/H GoF central hypoventilation/nonepileptic myoclonus without early seizures) against KCNT1 (Slack/Slo2.2 Na+-activated K+: GoF EIMFS with intra-ictal interhemispheric migrating focal seizures and severe ADSHE). Anchored to four verified RCSB PDB cryo-EM structures — 7CR0 (3.1 Å human KCNQ2 apo), 7CR2 (3.2 Å human KCNQ2 + retigabine FBX: H17–Phe305 2.32 Å, H16–Leu299 2.45 Å, H18–Ser303 2.48 Å, O3–Trp236 2.97 Å sparing cardiac KCNQ1 Leu266), 5U76 (3.76 Å Slo2.2 closed), and 5U70 (3.76 Å Slo2.2 open: His270–Phe214 4.01→3.40 Å tightening, RCK1 Val398 core 3.66–3.74 Å, RCK2 Pro897–RCK1 Asp363 4.05 Å strut). Includes two spoken calculation pauses (M-current dominant-negative binomial tetramer combinatorics 1−0.5^4=93.75% + chord-conductance/R_in EPSP threshold cliff; quinidine KCNT1 vs. cardiac hERG 16.7–100x inverted selectivity index), precision management (first-line NaV blockers in KCNQ2 LoF DEE; ezogabine phenazinium pigmentation withdrawal & XEN496 NCT04639310/NCT04912856 termination; ketogenic diet 62.5% / CBD 50% / cautious quinidine 44.6% in EIMFS), and emerging therapies (pigment-free Kv7 openers azetukalner/XEN1101 with TMS-EEG biomarkers and BHV-7000; oral hERG-sparing KCNT1 inhibitor ABS-1230 NCT07156201/NCT07600736 KYRON; intrathecal KCNT1 knockdown ASO S230815 NCT07227857 KANDLE; KCNQ2 SupRep AAV).

item.title: Benjamin Franklin (1706–1790) — Silence Dogood, the Electrical Kite, the Cockpit Ordeal, and the 1778 French Alliance
item.description: How a runaway Boston chandler's son franchised colonial printing, tamed lightning with a single-fluid theory, absorbed an hour of Privy Council mockery in silence, and wore a marten fur cap at Versailles to win the French fleet and broker the U.S. Constitution.

item.title: Theodore Roosevelt (1858–1919) — The Black Cross, the Badlands Pursuit, the Rough Riders, the Iron Trusts, the 84-Minute Bullet, and the River of Doubt
item.description: How a gasping Manhattan boy built his body on a second-floor porch, hunted boat thieves down the ice-choked Little Missouri while reading Tolstoy, hijacked the Navy telegraph to trigger Manila Bay, stared down J.P. Morgan to assert federal sovereignty, placed 230 million acres under protection, delivered an 84-minute speech with a .38 bullet in his chest, and nearly died mapping Brazil's uncharted River of Doubt.

item.title: Joseph Priestley & Carl Wilhelm Scheele (1733–1804 / 1742–1786) — Fire-Air, the Burning Lens, the Taste of Cyanide, and the Birmingham Riots
item.description: How a Yorkshire Dissenter beside a Leeds brewery and a freezing Swedish apothecary using pig bladders unlocked oxygen, chlorine, soda water, and ten new gases—only for slow printers, a candid Paris dinner, heavy-metal poisons, and a Bastille Day mob to cost them priority, health, and home.

item.title: Antoine-Laurent & Marie-Anne Lavoisier (1743–1794 / 1758–1836) — Tax-Farming Capital, Oxygen, 13 Copperplates, and the Widow's Revenge
item.description: How a Parisian tax-farmer and his brilliant thirteen-year-old bride armed the American Revolution with gunpowder, proved respiration is combustion, shattered Aristotle's four elements, engraved the bible of modern chemistry—and collided fatally with Jean-Paul Marat and the Reign of Terror.

item.title: John Dalton & Amedeo Avogadro (1766–1844 / 1776–1856) — Atomic Weights, the HO Trap, Diatomic Molecules, and Cannizzaro's Pamphlet
item.description: How a color-blind Cumberland Quaker schoolmaster weighed invisible atoms yet choked on water's formula, why a quiet Turin lawyer's 1811 diatomic solution was ignored for fifty years of chemical anarchy, and how a Sicilian revolutionary's pamphlet at Karlsruhe made the scales fall from Europe's eyes.

item.title: Justus von Liebig & William Henry Perkin (1803–1873 / 1838–1907) — The Five-Bulb Kaliapparat, the Mauve Attic, the One-Day Alizarin Race, and Coal-Tar Pharma
item.description: How a Darmstadt apothecary's son turned a Hessian police barracks into the modern PhD research lab and revolutionized agriculture—and how an 18-year-old East London apprentice hunting synthetic quinine spilled alcohol onto black aniline sludge, ignited the Mauve Decade, and watched Germany turn his coal-tar breakthrough into the modern pharmaceutical industry.

item.title: Kekulé, Couper & van 't Hoff (1829–1896 / 1831–1892 / 1852–1911) — The Clapham Omnibus, Wurtz's 26-Day Delay, Benzene's Snake, Kolbe's Pegasus, and the First Chemistry Nobel
item.description: How an architectural student seduced by Liebig at a murder trial daydreamed carbon chains and benzene's tail-biting snake while a Scottish rival lost priority by 26 days and vanished into silence—before a 22-year-old Dutch prodigy smashed chemistry into 3D space, humiliated Leipzig's angriest tyrant, and won the very first Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

item.title: Alexander Hamilton (1755–1804) — The 1772 Hurricane Letter, Yorktown Redoubt 10, the 1790 Bargain, and Weehawken
item.description: How an illegitimate Caribbean counting-house clerk wrote his way out of St. Croix after a hurricane, stormed Yorktown with unloaded muskets, built America's sovereign financial engine from bankruptcy, detonated his own career in the Reynolds Pamphlet, and fell on Weehawken's dueling ledge.

item.title: Thomas Jefferson (1743–1826) — Monticello, the Declaration, Paris & Sally Hemings, the Freneau Proxy War, and Louisiana
item.description: How a soft-spoken Virginia polymath drafted America's creed of liberty atop an enslaved estate, fled British dragoons from Monticello, waged covert proxy war against Hamilton via State Department payroll, abandoned strict construction to double the continent for $15 million, and died hours before John Adams on July 4, 1826.

item.title: George Washington (1732–1799) — Jumonville Glen, Trenton, the Newburgh Spectacles, Annapolis, and the Two-Term Precedent
item.description: How an ambitious Virginia surveyor who accidentally sparked the Seven Years' War mastered silent theatrical authority, kept a starving Revolution alive across the Delaware, disarmed a military coup by pulling out his spectacles, and weaponized the voluntary surrender of power to invent the American republic.

item.title: John & Abigail Adams (1735–1826 / 1744–1818) — The Boston Massacre Defense, 'Remember the Ladies,' Dutch Loans, and Defying War Hawks
item.description: How a stubborn Braintree lawyer and his razor-sharp Weymouth-born partner risked ruin to defend British redcoats, forged independence through 1,100 wartime letters and Dutch bank loans, endured a mutinous Hamiltonian cabinet, sacrificed re-election to stop an unnecessary war with France, and reconciled with Jefferson in luminous old age.

item.title: Abraham Lincoln (1809–1865) — New Salem Debt, the Freeport Trap, Team of Rivals, Emancipation, and the 13th Amendment
item.description: How a self-taught frontier flatboatman washed out of Congress over the Mexican War, returned to trap Stephen Douglas in 1858, brokered the Chicago Wigwam floor to win the presidency, waited for Antietam to unleash Emancipation, and twisted lame-duck arms with ruthless patronage to abolish slavery by two House votes.

item.title: Frederick Douglass (1818–1895) — The Stolen Alphabet, Edward Covey's Barnyard, the Corinthian Hall Thunder, and Confronting Lincoln
item.description: How an enslaved boy on Maryland's Eastern Shore traded bread for spelling lessons, whipped a slave-breaker in a two-hour barnyard fight, escaped north on a borrowed sailor's pass, defied white abolitionist patrons with his own press, confronted Lincoln inside the White House, and refused to bully Haiti beneath U.S. gunboats.

item.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt & Frances Perkins (1882–1945 / 1880–1965) — Triangle Fire, Steel Braces, Social Security, and the Arsenal of Democracy
item.description: How a paralyzed Hudson Valley patrician and the Worcester chemist seared by the Triangle Shirtwaist fire engineered hidden-disability stagecraft, broke the Great Depression with radio and a seven-point Cabinet ultimatum, built Social Security behind locked doors, and steered the Grand Alliance through World War II.

item.title: Lyndon B. Johnson (1908–1973) — Box 13, Master of the Senate, Civil Rights & Great Society, and the Vietnam Tragedy
item.description: How a Hill Country populist's son climbed from the Welhausen schoolroom and an 87-vote Box 13 miracle to rule the U.S. Senate through 'The Treatment,' pass the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Voting Rights Act, and Medicare, and fall inside the guns-and-butter tragedy of Vietnam.

item.title: Paracelsus & Jan Baptist van Helmont (1493–1541 / 1580–1644) — How a mine-raised Swiss firebrand burned Avicenna's Canon, formulated toxicology's law of the dose, and passed the chemical torch to a silenced Flemish nobleman who weighed a willow tree for five years, coined the word 'gas,' discovered gastric acid, and proved the conservation of matter.
item.description: How a mine-raised Swiss firebrand burned Avicenna's Canon, formulated toxicology's law of the dose, and passed the chemical torch to a silenced Flemish nobleman who weighed a willow tree for five years, coined the word 'gas,' discovered gastric acid, and proved the conservation of matter.

item.title: Robert Boyle & Robert Hooke (1627–1691 / 1635–1703) — The Earl's Son, the Orphan Mechanic, the Air-Pump, Micrographia, Phosphorus, and Newton's Wrath
item.description: How Ireland's richest aristocratic prodigy and a crooked-spined Isle of Wight servitor forged the pneumatic air-pump, Boyle's Law, modern chemistry, the biological cell, and London's post-fire skyline—before alchemy, cold urine-distilled phosphorus, and Isaac Newton's fury tore their legacies apart.

item.title: Humphry Davy (1778–1829) — Nitrous Oxide, Seven Voltaic Elements, Chlorine, the Miner's Lamp, and the Blackball
item.description: How a reckless Cornish woodcarver's son inhaled laughing gas with Romantic poets, electrified Regency London by tearing seven elements straight out of molten rock, refused to patent the coal-miner's safety lamp, and succumbed to toxic fumes and bitter jealousy over his own greatest discovery—Michael Faraday.

item.title: Michael Faraday (1791–1867) — 386 Bound Pages, the First Motor, Electrolysis Laws, Magnetized Light, and Lines of Force
item.description: How a Southwark blacksmith's son armed with one loaf of bread a week and zero university calculus rose from bookbinding to liquefy gases, isolate benzene, invent the electric motor and dynamo, quantize electrolysis, twist light with a magnet, refuse knighthood, and hand James Clerk Maxwell the invisible field universe.

item.title: Jöns Jacob Berzelius & Friedrich Wöhler (1779–1848 / 1800–1882) — The Chemical Alphabet, Isomerism, Protein, and Göttingen's 8,000 Chemists
item.description: How a Swedish orphan working beside his housekeeper's soup stove weighed 2,000 compounds, invented modern H₂O notation, and coined isomerism, catalysis, and protein—while his adopted German protégé synthesized biological urea from inorganic salts, united with rival Justus Liebig on bitter almonds, and trained 8,000 chemists across two continents.

item.title: Dmitri Mendeleev (1834–1907) — The 1,400-Mile Siberian Carriage, Chemical Solitaire, Gallium's Density Correction, Bigamy, and the 1906 One-Vote Nobel Snub
item.description: How a Siberian glassmaker's youngest son rode 1,400 miles across the Urals on his dying mother's last rubles, missed a cheese-dairy train to play solitaire with 63 element cards, boldly corrected a French discoverer's lab measurement from 1,500 miles away, survived Tsarist blackballing, and lost the 1906 Nobel Prize by one vindictive Stockholm vote.

item.title: Svante Arrhenius & Josiah Willard Gibbs (1859–1927 / 1839–1903) — Gibbs Free Energy, the 4th-Class Thesis, the 1896 CO₂ Calculation, and the Nobel Gatekeeper
item.description: How an unpaid New Haven bachelor wrote the thermodynamic bible of chemistry inside an unread Connecticut journal while a brash Swedish rebel nearly flunked his PhD over dissolved salt ions—then rallied Europe's young Ionists, hand-calculated CO₂ global warming in 1896, won the 1903 Chemistry Nobel, and turned Stockholm's Nobel committees into his personal fortress.

item.title: Marie Skłodowska Curie & Ernest Rutherford (1867–1934 / 1871–1937) — The Flying University, Pitchblende Cauldrons, Gold Foil, Two Nobels, and Splitting the Atom
item.description: How a Polish governess from Warsaw's secret Flying University boiled tons of Bohemian ore to isolate polonium and radium and survived Paris's xenophobic mobs to claim two Nobel Prizes—while a booming New Zealand farmboy proved radioactivity is atomic transmutation, bounced alpha shells off gold foil to reveal the atomic nucleus, and artificially split nitrogen.

item.title: Gilbert N. Lewis, Fritz Haber & R.B. Woodward (1875–1946 / 1868–1934 / 1917–1979) — Haber-Bosch, Ypres, the Covalent Bond, 41 Nobel Snubs, Vitamin B₁₂, and Orbital Symmetry
item.description: How Fritz Haber conjured 'bread from air' only to unleash chlorine gas at Ypres and perish exiled by the Nazis; how Gilbert N. Lewis invented the shared-electron-pair bond, Lewis acids, and heavy water yet died amid HCN fumes after 41 Nobel snubs; and how MIT flunk-out R.B. Woodward turned strychnine, chlorophyll, Vitamin B₁₂, and orbital symmetry into high architectural art.

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Neuropharmacology & Bioenergetics: Nicotinic Allostery, SARM1/NAMPT & Rescuing Axons After Blast TBI & Metabolic Stress
item.description: Five-Act historical and biophysical exploration of two intertwined neuropharmacological frontiers: (1) selective alpha-7 and alpha-4-beta-2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor allostery and desensitization in prefrontal cognitive dysfunction (from Loewi, Changeux & Freedman to Cincotta, Yorek MS et al. 2008 and modern PAM/muscarinic therapeutics), and (2) the Wallerian degeneration WldS/SARM1/NAMPT NAD+ survival switch—showing how subclinical pattern-ERG diagnostics after blast-mediated traumatic brain injury identify a therapeutic window where the NAMPT activator P7C3-S243 prevents chronic visual loss (Dutca, Pieper, Harper et al. 2014, PMC5102342) alongside NRK1/2 nicotinamide riboside salvage (Trammell, Brenner et al. 2016, PMC4882590).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Nociceptor Ion Channels: Complement C5a/C3a, TRPV1, TRPM8 & Tetrodotoxin-Resistant Na+ Channels in Pain
item.description: Five-Act biophysical journey from Bordet & Ehrlich's discovery of complement (1899), David Julius's cloning of TRPV1 (1997), Ardem Patapoutian's TRPM8 (2002), and Waxman/Wood's TTX-resistant nociceptor sodium channels (NaV1.8/NaV1.9) to collaborative studies revealing how C5a and C3a anaphylatoxins sensitize cutaneous heat and mechanical nociceptors via TRPV1 and NGF (Jang, Usachev, Brennan et al. 2010, Pain, PMC2814960), how natriuretic peptides vs IL-6 cytokines modulate cardiac nociceptive TRPV1 and TTXr-Na+ currents (Mohapatra, Usachev, Yorek MS 2011), and how corneal C-fiber TRPM8 osmosensing measures small-fiber integrity (PMC5113984).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Host Defense & Immunity: Leishmania CXCL1 Proteolysis, Neutrophil CD47/SHP-1 Brakes & CD4 Enhancer Demethylation
item.description: Five-Act immunological detective story tracing three fundamental checkpoints of innate and adaptive immunity: (1) from Mosmann & Coffman's 1986 Th1/Th2 Leishmania major paradigm to selective parasite metalloprotease cleavage of murine CXCL1 (PMC6625741) and the temporal IL-4 instruction paradox (PMC7640617); (2) from motheaten Ptpn6/SHP-1 mutant mice and Weissman's CD47 checkpoint to proving CD47 halts Ptpn6-deficient neutrophils from provoking lethal RIPK1/IL-1 autoinflammation (Science Advances 2023, PMC9821860); and (3) from Littman's Cd4 silencer/enhancer architecture and Rao's TET dioxygenases to stimulus-responsive DNA demethylation sustaining effector CD4 T-cell identity (Nature Communications 2022, PMC8933563).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Immunometabolism & Oncology: FABP4 & FABP5 Lipid Chaperones in Dietary Fat, Psoriasis, Ferroptosis & Metastasis
item.description: Five-Act immunometabolic and oncology synthesis tracing intracellular fatty acid-binding proteins from Robert Ockner's 1972 discovery, 10-stranded beta-barrel crystallography, Gokhan Hotamisligil's FABP4/aP2 metabolic-inflammation paradigm, and Brent Stockwell's discovery of ferroptosis (2012) to Bing Li's discovery of macrophage FABP4 vs FABP5 subset specialization—unpacking how FABP5 links dietary saturated vs omega-3 fats and the keratinocyte FABP5-VCP complex to cutaneous IL-36/NF-kB/IL-1b psoriatic inflammation (Cell Reports 2022, 2023, 2025), while FABP4-driven macrophage lipid accumulation and ATGL lipolysis fuel breast cancer metastasis (eLife 2024, PMC11548877) and omega-3 PUFAs trigger CD36/FABP5 tumor ferroptosis.

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Ion Channels & Gene Editing: NaV1.6 (SCN8A), Parvalbumin Interneuron Failure & Adenine Base Editing Rescue of Epilepsy
item.description: Five-Act biophysical and genetic capstone tracing voltage-gated sodium channels from Hodgkin & Huxley (1952), Catterall's DIII-DIV IFM fast-inactivation latch, Raman & Bean's resurgent Na+ current (1997), Miriam Meisler's cloning of Scn8a (NaV1.6) and discovery of human SCN8A developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (2012), and Gaudelli & David Liu's invention of CRISPR Adenine Base Editors (2017) to recent brain-slice electrophysiology proving how gain-of-function SCN8A drives parvalbumin interneurons into premature depolarization block and synaptic failure (Miralles, Patel et al. 2024 JCI Insight, PMC11529981) and in vivo AAV adenine base editing rewriting R1872W back to wild-type to rescue seizures and sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (Reever, Meisler, Farber, Patel et al. 2026 JCI, PMC12871382).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (I): The Scintillation Counter & the Fluid Membrane — Paul D. Ray, Art Spector & Docosahexaenoic Acid (1929–1989)
item.description: Episode I of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants legacy series honoring American biochemist Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek's 45-year career (1980–2026): from Bemidji State University (B.S. 1976; Outstanding Alumni Award 2003) and isolated perfused rabbit livers with Ph.D. mentor Paul D. Ray at the University of North Dakota (lineage of Nobel Laureate Edward A. Doisy and Henry A. Lardy) to postdoctoral work at Iowa with NIH-trained lipid pioneer Arthur A. Spector, culminating in the 1,501-citation classic Spector & Yorek (1985, J. Lipid Res.) proving how 22:6n-3 (DHA) remodels membrane fluidity, Eadie-Hofstee high-affinity neurotransmitter uptake, and receptor signaling.

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (II): The Sugar Decoy & the Sodium Pump — Myo-Inositol, SMIT & the L-Fucose Breakthrough (1973–1998)
item.description: Episode II of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants series honoring Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek: how Gabbay (1973) and Greene, Lattimer & Sima (1987, NEJM) framed the polyol-myo-inositol-Na+/K+-ATPase hypothesis of diabetic neuropathy, why human aldose reductase inhibitor trials faltered, and how Mark Yorek, Joyce A. Dunlap, and Lawrence J. Coppey used 3H-myo-inositol, ouabain-sensitive 86Rb+/22Na+ pump flux, Northern blots of SMIT mRNA, and the deceptive hexose L-fucose (J. Neurochem., JBC, Diabetes 1987–1998) to prove competitive transport inhibition, rescue nerve conduction velocity in diabetic rats, and discover why endothelial cells refused to behave like pure nerves.

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (III): Hanging the 60-Micron Vessel — Epineurial Arterioles & Why Nerves Starve Before They Die (1980–2006)
item.description: Episode III of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants series honoring Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek: building on Furchgott & Zawadzki (1980), Tuck, Schmelzer & Low (1984), and Peter J. Dyck (1985), Mark Yorek, Lawrence J. Coppey, Jill S. Gellett, Eric P. Davidson, and Donald D.istad/Heistad perfected pressurized videomicroscopy of 60–100 micron sciatic epineurial arterioles—proving via Poiseuille's r^4 law, laser Doppler endoneurial blood flow, acetylcholine (NO + EDHF) vs CGRP relaxation, and temporal time-course studies (Diabetes 2000–2003) that microvascular endothelial dysfunction precedes motor nerve conduction slowing.

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (IV): Superoxide, Peroxynitrite & the Vasopeptidase Shield — NEP, CGRP & Neurovascular Rescue (2000–2018)
item.description: Episode IV of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants series honoring Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek: dissecting the diffusion-limited collision of superoxide (O2.-) with nitric oxide (k ~ 1.9 x 10^10 M^-1 s^-1) to form peroxynitrite (ONOO-) inside epineurial arterioles (Coppey et al. 2001, Diabetes, 469 citations; Obrosova, Pacher, Szabo & Yorek collaborations on PARP-1 & FeTMPyP/MnTBAP, PMC5321249), and Yorek's pioneering discovery that upregulated neutral endopeptidase (NEP / neprilysin) degrades vasodilatory CGRP and natriuretic peptides—rescued by dual ACE/NEP vasopeptidase inhibition (AVE7688 / ilepatril, Diabetes, Hypertension, PMC2817866, PMC2933895) and genetic NEP-/- knockout mice (PMC7714044, co-authored with Matthew S. Yorek).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (V): A Window in the Living Eye — Corneal Nerves, Father–Son Studies, NR & the 2026 Human Blink Test
item.description: Episode V of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants series honoring Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek: the translational bridge from Rayaz A. Malik's corneal confocal microscopy (2003) and Iowa's VA Center for the Prevention and Treatment of Visual Loss (with Randy H. Kardon, Pieter Poolman, Charles Brenner, and Donna Hammond) to the 9 father–son papers co-authored by Matthew S. Yorek and Mark A. Yorek (2014–2016)—including the 490-citation Nicotinamide Riboside NAD+ discovery (Trammell et al. 2016, Scientific Reports, PMC4882590) and Matthew & Mark Yorek's 2016 invention of the TRPM8 hyperosmolar eye-drop squinting assay (IOVS, PMC5113984), culminating ten years later in Mark Yorek & Randy Kardon's 2026 human Type 2 diabetes validation (Cornea, PMID 42370874, ROC AUC = 0.90, Cohen's d = 1.46).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (VI): Forty Years Back to Omega-3 — Resolvin D1, Nerve Regeneration & Horizons to 2050
item.description: Episode VI (Grand Finale) of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants series honoring Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek's 45-year career (1980–2026): how the 1983–1985 DHA neural lipid discoveries with Art Spector came full circle 30–40 years later when Mark Yorek, Lawrence Coppey, Eric Davidson, Alexander Obrosov, and Matthew S. Yorek proved that omega-3 menhaden oil, 15-lipoxygenase-1 metabolites (Resolvin D1 / E1, neuroprotectin D1), and salsalate acetylation synergy don't merely slow diabetic neuropathy—they actively regenerate vanished corneal and intraepidermal nerve fibers, protect disuse skeletal muscle atrophy (2025, PMC12747565), establish rational combination therapy (2024–2025, PMC11133577, PMC12292556, PMC12341837), and inspire the 2026–2050 precision neurovascular regeneration era.

item.title: The First Dose That Slowed the Heart — Myriocin to Fingolimod-Phosphate S1P1 Agonism/Internalization (PDB 7EO4), Atrial GIRK First-Dose AV Block vs. Sustained Lymphocyte Sequestration & FREEDOMS/TRANSFORMS Trials
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 107: Myriocin to Fingolimod-Phosphate S1P1 Agonism/Internalization (PDB 7EO4), Atrial GIRK First-Dose AV Block vs. Sustained Lymphocyte Sequestration & FREEDOMS/TRANSFORMS Trials. At the sixth hour of a first fingolimod observation, an atrial impulse reaches the ECG and fails to reach the ventricles. Two weeks later, the lab reports a sharp fall in circulating lymphocytes. The Critical Care Clinician follows conduction, perfusion and the blood count. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows an active phosphate ester into a receptor and then follows the receptor off the lymphocyte surface. The patient, dialogue and individual values are fictional. David S. Miller’s “ABC Transporter Regulation by Signaling at the Blood–Brain Barrier” (2014) in the live Pharmacology notebook provides the rat brain-capillary starting point. Drug development, human trials and bedside interpretation draw on separate sources. Pharmacology notebook · Primary capillary experiment

The Molecular Pharmacologist reconstructs COMT discovery, magnesium coordination and the evidence for a possible mitochondrial liability. The patient, test values and dialogue are fictional. item.title: The Fracture the Scan Didn't Predict — Alendronate Hydroxyapatite Binding & Osteoclast FPPS Inhibition (PDB 2F92), FIT Hip Fracture Reduction, CTX/P1NP Turnover Markers & Atypical Subtrochanteric Femoral Fracture
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 117: Alendronate Hydroxyapatite Binding & Osteoclast FPPS Inhibition (PDB 2F92), FIT Hip Fracture Reduction, CTX/P1NP Turnover Markers & Atypical Subtrochanteric Femoral Fracture. A woman’s hip density improved during alendronate treatment. Seven years after she started, a new ache down the outside of her thigh brings her back. Follow the separate paths from a whole-region density measurement to a focal cortical injury, and from an oral tablet to a mineral surface and an enzyme inside an osteoclast. The starting chapter, *Bone and Joints* in the 2013 third edition of *Haschek and Rousseaux’s Handbook of Toxicologic Pathology*, includes alendronate in an ovariectomized rat model and discusses bone remodeling, markers and atypical fractures. Use the animal material for mechanism and the linked human sources for clinical outcomes. Pharmacology notebook

item.title: The Ovulation Signal and the Outcome — Enclomiphene vs. Zuclomiphene Isomer Kinetics, Estrogen Receptor Antagonist Conformation (PDB 6VPF), Timed Mid-Luteal Progesterone vs. PPCOS II Live-Birth Endpoints
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 118: Enclomiphene vs. Zuclomiphene Isomer Kinetics, Estrogen Receptor Antagonist Conformation (PDB 6VPF), Timed Mid-Luteal Progesterone vs. PPCOS II Live-Birth Endpoints. A follicle grows, the next scan shows it has collapsed, and progesterone rises. The Critical Care Clinician follows what each measurement establishes for a woman seeking pregnancy. The fertility episode draws on separate evidence in women. Historical sources use polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). The international guideline adopted polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) in its May 2026 terminology update. Pharmacology notebook · International guideline terminology update

item.title: The Drug That Had to Reach the Colon — Azad Khan's 1977 Sulfasalazine Split Experiment, pH-Dependent Eudragit & MMX Mesalamine Colonic Delivery, Fecal Calprotectin vs. Mucosal Endoscopy & Interstitial Nephritis Surveillance
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 120: Azad Khan's 1977 Sulfasalazine Split Experiment, pH-Dependent Eudragit & MMX Mesalamine Colonic Delivery, Fecal Calprotectin vs. Mucosal Endoscopy & Interstitial Nephritis Surveillance. An oral drug can reach the bloodstream and still deliver little to the tissue it is meant to treat. Mesalamine turns that problem into a historical experiment. First separate the two products of sulfasalazine, then find a way to bring the active one back to inflamed colonic mucosa. The starting source is Chapter Four, *Mucosal Healing in Ulcerative Colitis: Pathophysiology and Pharmacology*, in *Advances in Clinical Chemistry* (2013). Its discussion of 5-aminosalicylic acid and epithelial restitution leads into the original experiments. Pharmacology notebook

item.description: Visual attention, expert search, and perceptual awareness boundaries: Simons & Chabris's (1999) selective-attention paradigm, Drew et al.'s (2013) lung-nodule chest-CT experiment in which 20 of 24 radiologists missed an embedded gorilla despite majority eye-tracking fixation on its location, Wallisch et al.'s (2023) motion-speed boundary conditions, and Nartker et al.'s (2025) large-scale test of residual visual sensitivity.

item.description: Multiple human memory systems through quantitative testing of Patient H.M. item.description: Forensic personal identification via implanted medical devices: Hirt et al.'s (2018) Brno hip-prosthesis batch trace across four hospitals and 117 surgical records, Blessing & Lin's regional medical-examiner series on unique device serial numbers, skeletal radiographic matching, and ANSI/ASB Standard 148 (2024).

item.title: The Water the City Kept — Tikal Maya Corriental Crystalline Quartz & Zeolite Filtration, Cinnabar Mercury & Cyanobacterial eDNA Across Urban Reservoirs

item.description: Middle Paleolithic pyrotechnology and experimental archaeometry (#33): the Dutch North Sea Zandmotor Neanderthal tar-backed flint flake (Niekus et al. 2019), Kozowyk et al.'s (2017) experimental birch-bark tar yields across ash-mound, pit-roll, and raised-structure methods, Schmidt et al.'s (2021, 2023) lap-shear mechanical testing and FTIR/GC-MS comparison of the two Königsaue artifacts, and Kozowyk et al.'s (2023) biomarker equifinality limits.

item.description: Archaeoacoustics and prehistoric aerophone mechanics (#37): Fritz et al.'s (2021) CT and acoustic study of the modified Magdalenian Charonia lampas shell horn from Marsoulas Cave producing three near-harmonic pitches around C4–D#4, Kolar et al.'s (2012, 2022) in-situ architectural acoustics at Chavín de Huántar and Marsoulas Cave, and López-García et al.'s (2025) Catalonian Neolithic shell trumpets.

item.description: Epistemology of ancient script decipherment (#38): the May 1857 Royal Asiatic Society blind verification experiment comparing four sealed independent translations of the newly excavated Qalat Sherqat clay prism of Tiglath-Pileser I by Rawlinson, Hincks, Fox Talbot, and Oppert, Rassam's excavation record, polyvalent syllabic vs. logographic sign behavior, and line-by-line audit against the modern ORACC RIAo edition.

item.description: From nociceptor channel cloning to reversible peripheral nerve-ending remodeling: Caterina et al.'s (1997) expression cloning of the heat- and capsaicin-gated cation channel TRPV1, Kennedy et al.'s (2010) serial skin-punch biopsies quantifying ~80% reversible PGP 9.5 epidermal nerve-fiber loss and 24-week regeneration after a 60-minute 8% capsaicin patch, and contrasting Backonja (2008, low-dose active control in PHN) vs. Bischoff (2014, inert placebo in post-herniorrhaphy pain) RCT outcomes.

item.description: Cardiovascular-metabolic coupling in severe L-type calcium-channel blocker poisoning: Malakian et al.'s (2026) verapamil dysrhythmia and hypoinsulinemic hyperglycemia trajectory, Kline et al.'s (1993) controlled canine survival comparison of insulin-dextrose vs. calcium, epinephrine, and glucagon, Yuan et al.'s (1999) early human high-dose insulin euglycemic case series, and Cole et al.'s (2018) 199-patient poison-center chart review of hypoglycemia and hypokalemia risks.

item.title: The Drug That Changed With the Fever — Clozapine 1975 Finland Cluster & Kane 1988 Trial, Human H4–Gi Structure (PDB 8JXV), CYP1A2 Inflammation/Smoking Shift & AGP Binding
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 82: from the 1975 Finnish agranulocytosis cluster (Idänpään-Heikkilä et al.) and Kane et al.'s (1988) treatment-resistant schizophrenia trial (38/126 vs. 5/141) to ancillary human H4-Gi cryo-EM structure (PDB 8JXV), why acute pneumonia and abrupt smoking cessation elevate serum clozapine and the clozapine:norclozapine ratio via IL-6 CYP1A2 suppression and de-induction (Faber & Fuhr; Dickmann; Raaska), alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP) unbound-fraction buffering, and the June 2025 FDA clozapine REMS removal.

item.description: Gastrointestinal physiology and specimen physics of exocrine pancreatic testing: from Bayliss & Starling's (1902) secretin discovery and Burton et al.'s (1960) duodenal secretin-pancreozymin aspiration to endoscopic vs. tube bicarbonate crossover validation (Stevens et al. 2006), fecal elastase immunoassay validation (Löser et al. 1996), and Fischer et al.'s (2001) paired freeze-drying experiment showing 16/151 diarrheal stool samples normalize once corrected for water dilution.

item.title: How a Flash Test Separates the Retina’s Responses — Adrian's 1945 Red/Blue Scotopic-Photopic ERG, Dilated-Pupil Control, Miyake's Electronegative CSNB Waveform & ISCEV Standards

item.description: Biochemical kinetics and clinical laboratory physics of biotin immunoassay interference: Green's (1963) radiotracer measurement of avidin-biotin association/exchange, Bayer & Wilchek's (1974) affinity-capture chemistry, Trambas et al.'s (2018) paired serum biotin-spiking and streptavidin-depletion reversal experiments, and Li et al.'s (2017) human supplementation crossover demonstrating opposite interference directions in sandwich vs. competitive immunoassays.

item.title: The Seconds That Grew After the Fall — Stetson & Eagleman's 31-Meter Free-Fall Flicker Experiment, Oddball Predictability & Duration vs. Passage-of-Time Judgments
item.description: Experimental psychophysics of subjective time dilation and duration judgment: Stetson, Fiesta & Eagleman's (2007) 31-meter, 2.49-second free-fall experiment separating retrospective stopwatch expansion (2.96 s recalled vs. 2.17 s imagined, +36%) from unchanged wrist-LED flicker resolution, Pariyadath & Eagleman's (2007) visual oddball duration vs. pitch/flicker dissociation, and Martinelli & Droit-Volet's (2022, N=803) separation of numerical duration estimates from passage-of-time feelings.

item.title: The Spine That Looked Too Dense — Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DXA) Projection Geometry, Aortic Calcification & Contrast Artifacts, Vertebral Exclusions & ISCD Positions

item.title: The Tree That Stayed in the Timber — Forensic Timber STR & Chloroplast Profiling, Koompassia Log-to-Stump Matching, Shorea Databases & UNODC Likelihood Ratios

item.description: Biomolecular archaeology and microbial ecology of Bronze Age fermented dairy from the Tarim Basin: LC-MS/MS proteomics of Xiaohe tomb dairy lumps (Yang et al. 2014), dental calculus milk peptides in seven Xiaohe individuals despite lactase non-persistence genotypes (Zhang et al. 2021), ancient DNA capture and phylogeny of 3,500-year-old Lactobacillus kefiranofaciens strains (Liu et al. 2024), and experimental metabolic cross-feeding in modern kefir communities (Blasche et al. 2021).

item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 80: from Vakil's (1949) Rauwolfia root reports and Müller, Schlittler & Bein's (1952) reserpine isolation to V-ATPase 2H+:1 amine stoichiometry (Knoth et al.), human VMAT2-reserpine cytoplasm-facing cryo-EM coordinates (Wu et al. PDB 8JTC, Tyr341/Tyr433; Pidathala et al. PDB 8T6A), why noncovalent transporter blockade produces prolonged vesicular monoamine depletion and blunted orthostatic heart-rate compensation, and bounded interpretation of Freis's (1954) depression case series.

item.title: The Channel That Quieted Insulin — Congenital Hyperinsulinism Critical Samples, Diazoxide KATP Opening, SUR1/Kir6.2 Comparator (PDB 7W4O), KCNJ11 Genetics & Pulmonary Hypertension

item.title: The Antibiotic at the Other Ribosome — Linezolid Hyperlactatemia, Mitoribosome COX-II vs. Nuclear Tom20/SDHA Translation, Paired PBMC Recovery & Duration Cohort Denominators
item.description: Translational pharmacology and mitochondrial toxicology of oxazolidinone antibiotics: linezolid-associated hyperlactatemia despite 98% arterial oxygen saturation (Chaudhri et al. 2024, 4.9->5.1->1.6 mmol/L), selective depletion of mitoribosome-encoded cytochrome c oxidase subunits vs. nuclear-encoded Tom20 and SDHA in human HL-60/THP-1 cells (Milosevic et al. 2018), paired patient PBMC recovery (Garrabou et al. 2007, COX-II protein 16% and enzyme activity 51% of controls with intact mtDNA/mRNA), and 40-patient cross-sectional duration cohorts (Martínez-Guitián et al. 2026).

item.title: The Walk That Became a Seizure — Dalfampridine (4-AP) in Demyelinated Axons, Kv1.2/Kv2.1 Architecture (PDB 2R9R), Timed-Walk Trial Denominators & Renal Seizure Risk
